comment: I've read through a lot of the other comments and it seems there is little to add here, except to emphasize again the vagueness of her grading criteria and unclarity of her feedback. As the most concrete example I could give, for this course for the most of the semester I thought I would receive an A... In short, do NOT take her if you can.

Dr. Faulk is kind and very versed in sociology, but her class structure makes it difficult to enjoy the course. Rubrics are obscure, no helpful feedback is provided, and it seems like she grades just on vibes. Participation also makes or breaks your grade, and she posted her expectations (adapted from Harvard Graduate School) a week before finals.

I didn't like her as a professor, though others may feel differently. She bans using notes on technology of any sort because she wants her lecture slides hidden. That wouldn't normally be a problem except the course is broad, the slides are dense, and she's largely inaccessible outside of class. No feedback on papers or exam either but fun readings

Sooo...do not take this class. She originally gives very vague assignments, and two days before the assignment is due, gives us her rubric and guidelines. Also, she changes assignments and is a very harsh grader. She is condescending and has never answered questions.

DON'T TAKE an extremely harsh grader, lecture-heavy and doesn't share her slides; slides are so dense we're constantly missing material, never knows the answers to our questions, gives very unclear directions for assignments. Everyone failed the midterm. Sometimes I wish I were hit by an athlete on their electric scooter while heading to this class

Supposed to be an easy class but she grades so harshly. Midterm was extremely niche and had a million questions. I was surprised we even had to take a test considering its a sociology class and many things are subjective. She has not graded our essays or presentations that occurred during the first few months of the semester.

I began the class thinking it was great but the midterm came out of left field. The questions were niche and no one did well. She is hard to access outside of class and she grades things extremely harshly. In class participation is 35% of the grade and she was never satisfied with it. Her syllabus says that a B+ is really good work.

Firstly, the year is almost over and she has not graded our papers from the first month of school so I have no idea where my grade stands. There are also some mandatory but ungraded assignments which makes absolutely no sense. I also feel uncomfortable asking her questions as she often responds in a condescending/belittling manner. Don't take her
